messages:
Carlos (Acme): hey team — seeing a bunch of weird SSE behavior from our prod mobile users since last night. connections drop mid-stream, sometimes we get a partial final chunk (truncated sentence) and the client immediately reconnects and replays, which is doubling tokens billed on our end. attaching pcap and a short timeline: https://acme.gists/pcaps/stream-1803.pcap :disappointed:

Maya (Support): thanks Carlos. can you paste the exact curl/fetch you're using to reproduce? also any trace ids from the responses (X-Request-Id)?

Carlos (Acme): repro curl below. trace id I saw in one response: req_1803_ab12. curl:

```

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-13b"
```

Also here's the pcap: https://acme.gists/pcaps/stream-1803.pcap  — note the client (iOS) issues a reconnect every ~2s after drop, so it gets billed twice when the server replays final tokens.

Maya (Support): got it. I'm spinning up a repro from the pcap and will open an internal trace. filing internal support trace: sup-1803-01. pls hold.

Maya (Support): quick note — can you confirm whether you're setting any client-side SSE keepalive/heartbeat headers? some clients drop TLS when there's no activity for a few seconds.

Carlos (Acme): we don't send any explicit heartbeat. EventSource wrapper in our iOS client just listens and reconnects.

Maya (Support): ok thanks. preliminary from the pcap: I see the TCP connection receives a RST from the client ~18s after last server packet, and there's no explicit SSE "event: done" delivered. extracting relevant tcpdump lines now:

```

12:34:56.789 IP client.52012 > redwood.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567, ack 54321, win 229, length 222
12:35:14.902 IP redwood.443 > client.52012: Flags [.], seq 54321:54321, ack 12567, win 512, length 0  # keepalive probe
12:35:15.001 IP client.52012 > redwood.443: Flags [R], seq 12567, ack 54321, win 0

```

Maya (Support): that RST lines up with the missing final SSE payloads. sending these findings to eng. @Jin @Lina can you weigh in on whether the server is closing connections or if this looks client-side?

Lina (eng-sre): looking at metrics around the time window Carlos shared (2025-11-03T04:32:xx UTC) — we see a spike in streaming.connection.abrupt_close_count and streaming.p95_latency for tokenization (likely the final chunk processing) — query:

```

sum(increase(streaming_connection_abrupt_close_total[5m])) by (reason)
-> 53 (reason=client_reset)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(streaming_response_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) -> 1.2s (baseline ~0.3s)

```

Lina (eng-sre): also noticed a small uptick in ephemeral auth failures (auth.token_expiry) around the same window, but not enough to explain the volume.

Jin (eng-runtime): thanks, digging in. the runtime has a new default idle_heartbeat_timeout=10s that rolled out in last week's patch (intended to close truly idle connections). I suspect this interacts badly with some clients that pause output for >10s while finalizing generation; the runtime emits a keepalive probe but if the client resets (RST) while the server is mid-chunk we lose the final tokens and the resumed request gets billed separately because resume isn't deduped in billing.

Jin (eng-runtime): patch for canary I propose (one-line):

```

- if (idle_since > idle_heartbeat_timeout) close_connection();
+ if (idle_since > idle_heartbeat_timeout && !generation_in_progress()) close_connection();

```

Jin (eng-runtime): that should avoid closing while model is still emitting. I'll also add a resume_id header on resume attempts so billing can dedupe.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/streaming-v2 fix -> canary 3% -> 30% -> 100% (ETA 20m) :rocket:

Maya (Support): while that's rolling, quick mitigation for Carlos: can you try adding a client-side SSE keepalive that sends an empty HTTP POST or small ping every 8s, or at least set an EventSource-level reconnection backoff (jitter) so we avoid a tight replay loop? also if you can capture another pcap after the canary we can compare.

Carlos (Acme): ok trying. any headers I should send to let server resume instead of replay?

Jin (eng-runtime): after the canary lands we'll accept "Last-Event-ID" or a custom "X-Resume-Id" header; if you include it the server will resume from the KV cache and mark the billing record with resume_id to prevent double charges. temporary: use exponential backoff (start 1s, max 5s) + jitter.

Maya (Support): example repro curl to keep the TLS alive while you test:

```

# keep connection open, show SSE events as they arrive
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-13b" | sed -u 's/^/sse: /'
# for resume testing include Last-Event-ID header
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Last-Event-ID: resume_abc123" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-13b"
```

deploy-bot: runtime/streaming-v2 fix -> canary 3% successful, promoting to 30% :white_check_mark:

Carlos (Acme): tested with a patched client (added ping) against the canary region and saw far fewer truncations — still saw one instance where final punctuation missing but much improved. attaching new pcap: https://acme.gists/pcaps/stream-1803-after.pcap

Maya (Support): thanks — can you also paste the client side logs around the reconnect? that one instance might still be client RST'ing while server is mid-chunk.

Carlos (Acme): client log: "EventSource: connection reset by peer during read, reconnecting. lastEventId=resume_abc123"

Jin (eng-runtime): ok that line confirms: client RST during server stream finalization. two followups from runtime: 1) widen heartbeat timeout to 20s by default for now, 2) ensure resume_id dedupe in billing (hotfix queued).

Lina (eng-sre): I've created an alert to detect elevated resume-replay billing deltas and a dashboard panel showing streaming_reconnect_rate and resume_dedupe_hits.

Maya (Support): Carlos — leaving this open. please try the canary region for 24 hours with the keepalive and exponential reconnect jitter. if you still see truncations, reply with the new pcap and lastEventId; we'll escalate immediately. thanks for the great repro artifacts :pray: 

Carlos (Acme): will do, thanks Maya, Jin, Lina. appreciate the quick turn. :thumbsup:
